basis: First review after edit (edit pass_seq 1, verify-questions pass). sync 15 run first (written=0, unchanged=12). Skim pass of 1-fast.md and 2-deep.md (headings, bold, tables, captions), then full read of 1-fast.md, 2-deep.md, 3-do.md, 4-say.md, 5-quiz.md, sources.md (head) and data/15-cloudfront/{questions,cards,speak,tasks}.json, as the reader in READER.md. Facts checked in facts/cloudfront.md, facts/global-accelerator.md, facts/acm.md.

findings.section: Cache headers decide how long a copy lives and versioned names replace it sooner
findings.quote: AWS says to [use invalidation only in unexpected circumstances](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-invalidate-only-unexpected-use-versioning), and daily invalidations soon use up the free paths.
findings.evidence: Fact cloudfront-invalidation-first-1000-paths-free: 'The first 1,000 invalidation paths that you submit per month are free'. Fact cloudfront-invalidation-wildcard-counts-one-path (linked in the Go deeper block of this same subsection): a wildcard path 'counts as one path'. One daily /* invalidation is about 30 paths a month, far below 1,000, so the stated cause is wrong. The chapter contradicts itself: speak item cloudfront-s03 says 'The thing to watch is the real reason. It isn't mainly cost. A wildcard path counts as one path', and question cloudfront-q015 rejects the /* option for the browser/proxy reason, not for cost. The real AWS reason is in fact cloudfront-invalidation-prefer-versioning-for-frequent-updates (claim: 'versioning controls what a request returns even when users have a version cached locally or behind a corporate proxy'). Replace the clause with that reason (invalidation does not reach copies in browsers and corporate proxies). Same defect in the A-list row, see exam-01.
findings.resolution: fix-15: the clause is replaced by the browser and proxy reason (same fix as claims-01).

findings.section: CloudFront encrypts two separate connections and each one has its own setting
findings.quote: Why two settings? CloudFront [terminates TLS close to viewers](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-pricing-page-dynamic-acceleration-mechanisms) and opens a new TLS connection to the origin.
findings.evidence: The second clause has no fact link and is not in the linked fact: cloudfront-pricing-page-dynamic-acceleration-mechanisms quotes 'CloudFront terminates TLS close to viewers from distributed edge locations, maintains persistent connections to your origin'. It is also wrong in the case the table right above shows: row 'Redirect HTTP to HTTPS | HTTP | No' means the origin connection is not TLS at all. This is the one sentence that explains the cause (two legs), so it must be exact. Rewrite: CloudFront ends the viewer's TLS connection at the edge and makes a second, separate connection to the origin; the origin protocol policy decides whether that second connection uses HTTPS.
findings.resolution: fix-15: same fix as claims-05: a separate connection to the origin, with the protocol that the origin protocol policy sets.

findings.section: CloudFront and Global Accelerator: do it
findings.quote: Nothing here yet.
findings.evidence: 3-do.md and 4-say.md both print only 'Nothing here yet.' because all 4 tasks (cloudfront-t01 to t04), all 4 speak items (cloudfront-s01 to s04) and all 32 cards in data/15-cloudfront/ still have status 'candidate'. TOOLS-items.md: 'Only items with status: ready are printed'. TOOLS-rules.md R5: 'A reviewer sets cards, speak items and tasks to ready in the stage of that kind, after the item lint is clean.' The reader meets the gap four times: 1-fast 'Look first' has an empty task region (cloudfront-t01), and three 'Try it' callouts in 2-deep ('See [3-do.md](3-do.md)', tasks t02, t03, t04) lead to an empty page. Set the items ready with tasks/speak/cards set-status after their lint, then sync (same defect and fix as reader-02 of chapter 14).

findings.section: In one breath
findings.quote: Global Accelerator gives [two IPv4 static IP addresses](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-two-static-ipv4-independent-network-zones) for [both TCP and UDP protocols](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-protocols-tcp-and-udp).
findings.evidence: This is the sentence she will say to founders, and it names only the addresses, not what the service does with the traffic. A founder's next question is 'and then what?'. The mechanism is a verified fact: global-accelerator-anycast-nearest-edge-then-closest-endpoint, 'Global Accelerator routes traffic to the closest edge location by using Anycast, and then routes it to the closest regional endpoint over the AWS global network.' Add the second half (for example: 'and carries the traffic over the AWS global network to the closest healthy Region'), linked to that fact. READER.md: 'Every chapter gives her sentences she can say: a one-breath definition'.
findings.resolution: fix-15: Say it now reads 'CloudFront caches content near users. Global Accelerator gives two IPv4 static IP addresses and carries TCP or UDP over the AWS global network.' (the callout limit is 25 words, so the anycast link stays in 2-deep step 2).

findings.section: CloudFront encrypts two separate connections and each one has its own setting
findings.quote: Many think that HTTPS for viewers also covers the origin. CloudFront returns objects [regardless of whether the protocol used](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-https-viewer-origin-protocol-independent) for the origin matched.
findings.evidence: The second sentence is not grammatical ('regardless of whether the protocol used for the origin matched' has no object of 'matched') and does not say what happens. A second-language reader under time pressure cannot recover the meaning. Fact cloudfront-https-viewer-origin-protocol-independent: 'CloudFront will return an object to a viewer regardless of whether the protocol used by the viewer (HTTP or HTTPS) matches the protocol that CloudFront used to get the object.' Say the effect: 'A viewer can get an object over HTTPS that CloudFront fetched from the origin over HTTP: CloudFront returns it [regardless of whether the protocol used] by the viewer matches.' Question cloudfront-q006 uses a clearer wording ('toward the origin matches the viewer's').
findings.resolution: fix-15: now 'CloudFront can return an object to a viewer over HTTPS that it fetched from the origin over HTTP.'

findings.section: VPC origins let CloudFront reach load balancers and instances in private subnets
findings.quote: 3. **Keep a gateway.** [You need to add an internet gateway](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-vpc-origin-needs-internet-gateway) to the VPC.
findings.evidence: The subsection's point is 'no public address, a direct caller has nothing to reach', and step 3 then requires an internet gateway with no reason. The reader will conclude the origin is reachable from the internet after all, the opposite of the lesson. The same verified fact has the missing half as a display: cloudfront-vpc-origin-needs-internet-gateway, 'The internet gateway is required to denote that the VPC can receive traffic from the internet. The internet gateway is not used for routing traffic to origins inside the subnet, and you don't need to update the routing policies.' Add: it only marks the VPC as able to receive internet traffic and is [not used for routing traffic to origins inside] the subnet. The Say it line ('The thing to watch is the internet gateway') then makes sense.
findings.resolution: fix-15: same fix as claims-07: the gateway does not route traffic to the subnet, and the subnet stays private.

findings.section: VPC origins let CloudFront reach load balancers and instances in private subnets
findings.quote: A load balancer that must stay internet-facing leads to a prefix list and a custom header. Anything else leads to custom headers or origin mutual TLS.
findings.evidence: The ladder diagram (alt text and labels 'Prefix list and header', 'Header or origin mTLS') names three origin locks that 2-deep never explains: the CloudFront managed prefix list (only in the 1-fast Changed recently entry and decision record step 4), a secret custom origin header, and origin mutual TLS (never mentioned in prose). READER.md: 'Headings, tables and captions must give a correct gist on their own'; a diagram label she cannot decode gives no gist. The verified facts exist: elb-alb-cloudfront-prefix-list-sg, cloudfront-prefix-list-origin-facing-servers, cloudfront-alb-restrict-custom-header-and-https, cloudfront-faq-origin-mtls-replaces-allowlists-headers (named in the diagram spec notes). Add two short steps or a table under the figure: prefix list in the security group (blocks non-CloudFront addresses) plus a secret header checked by a listener rule (blocks other distributions). Question cloudfront-q012 tests exactly this; see exam-03.
findings.resolution: fix-15: under the ladder figure: 'An internet-facing ALB needs two locks. Its security group allows the AWS-managed prefix list for CloudFront. And CloudFront can add a custom HTTP header to requests, which a listener rule checks. Why both? The CloudFront managed prefix list contains the IP ranges of all CloudFront servers, so other customers' distributions pass it too.' Origin mTLS stays a ladder label only (word limit of 2-deep.md).

findings.section: Signed URLs and signed cookies decide which users can fetch private files
findings.quote: | An IP range | Custom policy: [you can specify the IP address or range](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-signed-policy-canned-only-expiry) |
findings.evidence: 'Custom policy' appears here for the first and only time; the canned policy it contrasts with is never named, and nothing says that the policy is part of the signed URL. Fact cloudfront-signed-policy-canned-only-expiry (claim): 'A canned policy for a signed URL can set only the date and time after which access ends; a custom policy can also set a start time (optional) and the IP address or range of allowed users (optional).' Add one sentence before the table: a signed URL carries a policy; a canned policy sets only the end time, a custom policy can also limit the start time and the IP range. Speak item cloudfront-s01 follow-up relies on the same idea.
findings.resolution: fix-15: before the table: 'A signed URL carries a policy. In a canned one, You can specify the date and time when access ends. A custom one adds a start time and an IP range.' (linked to cloudfront-signed-policy-canned-only-expiry).

findings.section: CloudFront Functions do light rewrites and edge Lambda functions can call other services
findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** A function must set a header on the origin's response from a pricing API. Which product fits? ... Lambda@Edge: CloudFront Functions do not run on origin events and have no [network access]
findings.evidence: Two problems. (1) The question is ambiguous in English: 'the origin's response from a pricing API' can mean the origin is a pricing API, or the function must call one. (2) The first reason in the answer teaches a false cause: setting a header on a response does not need an origin event, because CloudFront Functions run on the viewer response event (1-fast compare table: 'Viewer request and viewer response'; fact cloudfront-functions-use-cases lists header manipulation). The only deciding reason is the network call (fact cloudfront-functions-no-network-no-body-fs-access: 'Network access | No | Yes'). Rewrite the prompt as 'A function must call a pricing API and put the price in a response header' and answer with the network reason only.
findings.resolution: fix-15: prompt and answer rewritten as proposed.

findings.section: Cache headers decide how long a copy lives and versioned names replace it sooner
findings.quote: 3. **Check after expiry.** The origin answers [304 Not Modified](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-expiration-304-not-modified-revalidation) or sends the new file.
findings.evidence: The step names the origin's answer but not the question: who asks, and what happens to the cached copy. Rule (reviewer brief): a mechanism must be explained as cause and effect. Say it in order: after the TTL ends, CloudFront asks the origin whether the file changed; if not, the origin answers 304 Not Modified and CloudFront keeps serving its copy; if yes, the origin sends the new file. Fact cloudfront-expiration-304-not-modified-revalidation is already linked.
findings.resolution: fix-15: step 3 now 'CloudFront asks the origin if the file changed. 304 Not Modified keeps the copy; otherwise the new file comes back.'

findings.section: The cache key decides which requests share one cached copy
findings.quote: The share [served directly from the CloudFront cache](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-cache-hit-ratio-definition) is the **cache hit ratio**.
findings.evidence: 'The share' is read first as the verb from the previous sentence ('Requests with the same key share one copy'), then as a noun meaning 'proportion'. For a second-language reader this definition of a key exam term does not parse. STYLE: one term per concept, plain words. Write: 'The cache hit ratio is the percentage of requests that CloudFront [served directly from the CloudFront cache].'
findings.resolution: fix-15: now 'The cache hit ratio is the percentage of requests served directly from the CloudFront cache.'

findings.section: Requests reach the nearest edge location and cache misses travel on to the origin
findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** Two nearby users request the same new file at the same moment. How many requests reach the origin? ... One.
findings.evidence: Fact cloudfront-request-collapsing (claim): 'If additional requests for the same object (with the same cache key) arrive at an edge location before CloudFront receives the response to the first request, CloudFront pauses ...'. The answer holds only for the same edge location and the same cache key; 'nearby users' can be served by two edge locations. Also the table row above links the text 'this brief pause helps to reduce the load', but no pause has been described, so 'this' points to nothing. Write 'Two users reach the same edge location ...' and describe the pause in the table cell (for example: 'One: CloudFront holds the second request until the first answer arrives').
findings.resolution: fix-15: the prompt now says 'Two users reach the same edge location ...'. The table with the dangling 'this' was removed for the word limit (claims-17).

findings.section: Check
findings.quote: **Check 3.** A team ships new JavaScript files every day, and users keep getting old copies. What is the recommended fix?
findings.evidence: READER.md: 'Headings, tables and captions must give a correct gist on their own; questions must test what the gist misses.' On the skim pass every Check and Recap item of 1-fast is answered by a table row: Check 1 by Signals row 'S3 files only through CloudFront' and Trap 1; Check 2 by Signals row 'UDP, gaming, allow-list static IP addresses'; Check 3 by Signals row 'frequent updates, users see the old version'; Recap 1 to 3 by the three compare tables. Keep one recall item, and turn at least one Check into a twist the table does not hold (for example: the files are in an S3 website endpoint, so OAC does not apply; or the old copies sit in browsers, so an invalidation does not help).
findings.resolution: fix-15: Check 3 is now a twist that no table row holds: worldwide uploads to one bucket; the answer is S3 Transfer Acceleration (s3-transfer-acceleration-when-to-use), not CloudFront. Also covers exam-04.

findings.section: Check
findings.quote: **Check 1.** Photos are in a private S3 bucket. What lets the bucket answer the distribution and nobody else?
findings.evidence: 'answer the distribution' is not plain English for 'serve files to the distribution' and is hard to parse for a second-language reader (STYLE: plain English, no idioms). Write: 'What lets the distribution read the files while nobody else can?'
findings.resolution: fix-15: now 'What lets the distribution read the files, but nobody else?' ('while' is a warn word).

findings.section: CloudFront encrypts two separate connections and each one has its own setting
findings.quote: The ALB can keep its own: [import the certificate in any AWS Region](../facts/acm.md#acm-cloudfront-origin-certificate-any-region).
findings.evidence: The scenario says the team requested the ALB certificate in eu-west-1, and the answer link says 'import', so the reader may think an origin certificate must be imported. Fact acm-cloudfront-origin-certificate-any-region: 'you can request or import the certificate in any AWS Region.' Ask for the display 'request or import the certificate in any AWS Region' (facts request --display) or reword so the link text matches the case.
findings.resolution: fix-15: the TLS Spot the bug was removed (see claims-03).

findings.section: CloudFront Functions do light rewrites and edge Lambda functions can call other services
findings.quote: > **Say it:** The short answer is: CloudFront Functions for small rewrites, Lambda@Edge for network calls. The thing to watch is the extra latency.
findings.evidence: The subsection never says that Lambda@Edge adds latency; it says only that CloudFront Functions run in submillisecond time and Lambda@Edge 'for up to 30 seconds'. A sentence she says out loud should rest on what she just learned, and 'extra latency' invites a follow-up she cannot answer. Use a point the section teaches, for example 'The thing to watch is the price: CloudFront Functions cost a fraction of Lambda@Edge' (fact cloudfront-dec-functions-cheaper-than-lambda-edge), or 'whether the code needs the network'.
findings.resolution: fix-15: now 'The thing to watch is whether the code needs the network.'

findings.section: cloudfront-s04
findings.quote: If a key in the function can check the token, use CloudFront Functions. If the check must call your user service, use Lambda@Edge.
findings.evidence: 'a key in the function' is ambiguous when spoken: a signing key, a key-value pair, or a key of the code? The 60-second answer later mentions KeyValueStore, which makes it worse. A 10-second answer must be safe to say under stress (READER.md). Say: 'If the function can check the token's signature by itself, use CloudFront Functions. If the check must call your user service, use Lambda@Edge.'
findings.resolution: fix-15: now 'If the function can check the token from the request alone, use CloudFront Functions. ...' (no signature claim beyond fact cloudfront-dec-functions-use-token-validation).

findings.section: Signals and traps
findings.quote: | "S3 files only through CloudFront" | origin access control | ... | an S3 website endpoint, [also considered a custom origin](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-oac-s3-website-endpoint-not-supported) |
findings.evidence: The 'But not if' cell says what the website endpoint is, not what follows from it, and the reader does not know what 'custom origin' implies here. Fact cloudfront-oac-s3-website-endpoint-not-supported: 'That means you can't use OAC (or OAI).' Write the consequence with the fact display: 'an S3 website endpoint: [you can't use OAC (or OAI)]'.
findings.resolution: fix-15: cell now 'an S3 website endpoint, also considered a custom origin, so no OAC' (the contraction display was avoided).

findings.section: Decision record
findings.quote: 4. Dynamic requests go to the load balancer, whose security group allows the CloudFront prefix list.
findings.evidence: Two issues. (1) Lint W201: 'Decision record has 360 words; the section allows 0 to 280' (ledger warnings). (2) The record locks the load balancer with an internet-facing ALB plus the prefix list, while the same chapter calls VPC origins 'the newest and recommended solution' (fact cloudfront-dec-ddos-wp-vpc-origins-newest-recommended) and q017 picks a VPC origin. The record gives no reason for the choice, so the reader sees the book contradict itself. Either add one short trade-off line (why Callvale keeps the internet-facing ALB at month 11) or drop the prefix-list step; cut the repeated story sentences of the two step lists to get under 280 words.
findings.resolution: fix-15: step 4 now names the prefix list and a secret header; the trade-off adds 'The load balancer stays internet-facing; a VPC origin can come later.' Alt texts, captions and steps were shortened in the specs and the Markdown; the section went from 360 to about 310 words (W201 still warns, a warning only).

findings.section: FAQ quick-fire
findings.quote: > "There is no additional charge to use a custom origin."
findings.evidence: Three FAQ quotes do not answer their question. FAQ 1 asks 'Can CloudFront use an origin outside AWS?' and quotes the charge sentence; the fact cloudfront-faq-custom-origin-any-server-no-charge has the answering sentence 'Amazon CloudFront works with any origin server that holds the original, definitive versions of your content, both static and dynamic.' FAQ 8 asks whether example.com can point to a distribution and quotes 'Route 53 doesn't charge for queries to ALIAS records ...'; fact cloudfront-faq-zone-apex-route53-alias holds 'you can configure an ALIAS record that lets you map the apex or root (example.com) of your DNS name to your Amazon CloudFront distribution.' FAQ 9 quotes a sentence that starts with 'Second,' out of context; fact global-accelerator-faq-single-region-static-ip-benefits holds the 'First, ... onboarding their traffic onto the AWS global network' sentence that the answer cites. RULINGS: FAQ quick-fire 'with verbatim FAQ quotes'; the quote is the proof of the answer.
findings.resolution: fix-15: FAQ 1 now asks 'Does an origin outside AWS cost extra?' and its quote answers it. FAQ 9 now answers 'you can move it between Regions without changing your public interface', which the 'Second, ...' quote proves. FAQ 8 keeps the ALIAS charge quote, which names ALIAS records mapped to a CloudFront distribution; the longer apex quote did not fit the 4,500-word limit.

findings.section: cloudfront-c032
findings.quote: In Global Accelerator, a stateful application needs each user to reach the same endpoint. What do you set? / Client affinity by source IP address.
findings.evidence: The card's section is 2-deep.md#health-checks-and-traffic-dials-move-new-connections-from-one-region-to-another, but client affinity appears nowhere in the chapter prose. A card should recall what a section taught; this one introduces a new feature in Anki with no explanation. Either add one step or table row on client affinity to that subsection (fact global-accelerator-client-affinity-for-stateful-apps is verified) or retire the card.
findings.resolution: fix-15: the health-check subsection now says 'For a stateful application, client affinity set to Source IP can route the user to the same endpoint whenever they connect.' (global-accelerator-client-affinity-source-ip-uses-2-tuple). The card stays (C201 needs 32 hand cards).

findings.quote: Why can the edge cost less? A cache hit is a request that the origin does not serve.
findings.evidence: The answer explains less origin load, not a lower bill; the cost link (fewer instances, and the free origin fetch of step 1) is left for the reader to build. Add the second half: 'so the origin needs fewer instances, and the fetch from an AWS origin is free.'

findings.section: Global Accelerator carries TCP and UDP from two static addresses over the AWS network
findings.quote: Players send UDP game traffic to two Regions. The internet adds jitter, and partners' firewalls need fixed addresses.
findings.evidence: STARTUP.md: 'Stage 4: AWS Global Accelerator for live audio' and 'AWS Global Accelerator for live audio' under Edge. Both GA subsections use a game example only; the reader's running story never meets GA. One sentence ('Later, Callvale's live audio uses the same pattern') would tie the service to the story she will retell.
findings.resolution: fix-15: not applied for the 4,500-word limit of 2-deep.md (L201). Global Accelerator for live audio is a stage 4 event in STARTUP.md and belongs to the chapter that tells stage 4.
